sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: By giving strangers across the world a common table at which to sit and speak, online forums have quietly dissolved the walls of distance and prejudice that once kept us apart. （议论文·科技与联结）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: By doing结构点明方式 + 隐喻(common table / walls of distance)化抽象为具体 + 'quietly dissolved'拟人化动词强化论证感染力

translation: 专家，行家；熟练的，内行的，专家的
sub_section: A 句子类型探究
original_sentence: Users are encouraged to post their problems, and they will get advice from our health experts and other forum users.
readingExamples: Users are encouraged to post their problems, and they will get advice from our health experts and other forum users.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a person with a high level of knowledge or skill in a particular field, gained through training or experience
(2) adj. having or showing special skill or knowledge because of training or experience
(3) adj. done with, involving, or requiring great skill and knowledge

posExamples.sentence: The old carpenter said little, but the instant his expert hands touched the cracked violin, the boy knew his grandfather's last gift would somehow be saved. （读后续写·匠人·希望）
Users are encouraged to post their problems on the website, where they will receive advice from our health experts and other friendly forum users. （应用文·平台介绍·教材延伸）
With one expert glance the doctor read what a dozen tests had failed to show, and only then did the family dare to hope again. （读后续写·专业·转机）
We should not blindly trust every expert, for even the wisest can be wrong; true understanding grows only when we dare to question those who claim to know. （议论文·权威与独立思考）

collocations.example: Though only a village teacher, she was, in the eyes of every child there, the greatest expert on kindness the world had ever known. （读后续写·致敬·温情）
A leading expert on climate change warned that the choices we make today will echo for a hundred years. （议论文·环保）

collocations.phrase: consult / seek advice from an expert
collocations.example: If the problem troubles you deeply, do not hesitate to consult an expert rather than suffer in silence. （应用文·建议信）
Armed with expert advice from her coach, she stepped onto the field with a calm she had never felt before. （读后续写·比赛·自信）
Years of caring for her ailing mother had made her an expert at hiding her own exhaustion behind a smile. （读后续写·亲情·坚韧）
We are honoured to have invited an expert in her field to give us a talk on healthy eating. （应用文·活动通知）

collocations.translation: 以内行的眼光/娴熟的手法
collocations.example: With an expert eye, the old fisherman studied the sky and declared that a storm would break before nightfall. （读后续写·经验·预兆）
A medical expert reminded us that a good night's sleep does more for our health than any pill. （议论文·健康）

synonyms.translation: 专家，专科医生（专攻某狭窄领域者）
synonyms.example: The family doctor, sensing something serious, referred the child to a heart specialist at once. （读后续写·就医）
synonyms.usage: 强调专注于某一狭窄、专门领域（尤指医学分科）；expert 泛指在某领域技艺高超者，领域可宽可窄，语气更口语通用。

synonyms.example: She was a world authority on ancient languages, yet she never spoke down to the youngest student. （议论文/读后续写·学者）
synonyms.usage: 强调因权威地位而被公认为最可信的意见来源，庄重、正式；expert 更侧重实际的知识与技能，不必然带有'权威地位'的含义。

synonyms.example: Under the master's patient eye, the clumsy apprentice slowly grew into a craftsman himself. （读后续写·师承）
synonyms.usage: 多指技艺（手工、艺术、武术等）达到炉火纯青境界的大师，带敬仰色彩；expert 更中性，可用于任何知识或技能领域。

synonyms.example: He played the piano not as a hobbyist but as a true professional, every note precise and alive. （读后续写·才华）
synonyms.usage: 强调以此为职业、达到职业水准，与'业余'相对；expert 强调知识技能之精深，不必然以此谋生，二者常可并存。

advancedExpressions.expression: with the calm assurance of an expert, sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: With the calm assurance of an expert, she cleaned and bound the wound, and for the first time that terrible night, the room began to breathe again. （方式状语用职业从容感反衬危机，为情节带来转机）

advancedExpressions.expression: should you need further help, our experts are always ready to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Should you need further help along the way, our experts are always ready to offer advice with patience and care. （倒装虚拟条件句，礼貌而正式地承诺支持）

advancedExpressions.expression: even the greatest experts are not beyond question, for ...
advancedExpressions.example: Even the greatest experts are not beyond question, for knowledge advances precisely when someone dares to doubt what everyone else accepts. （让步结构+for引导原因，倡导独立思考而非盲信权威）

sentenceUpgrade.original: An expert helped us solve the problem.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Just as we were about to give up, an expert arrived — quiet, unhurried, sure — and with a few careful words untangled in minutes the problem that had defeated us for weeks. （读后续写·绝境·援手）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Just as...about to give up制造危机顶点 + 破折号三个形容词(quiet, unhurried, sure)速写人物气场 + 'weeks vs minutes'时间对比凸显专业

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should listen to experts, but also think for ourselves.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: While the guidance of experts can light our way, it must never replace the lamp of our own judgement; to follow blindly is to walk in another's shadow rather than to find our own path. （议论文·权威与独立）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: While引导让步 + 隐喻(light our way / lamp of judgement / another's shadow)贯穿全句 + 分号连接双分句形成对照，说理形象有力

translation: 可能的，预料的，有希望的
sub_section: A 句子类型探究
original_sentence: It is likely that the matter has already been discussed on our forum.
readingExamples: It is likely that the matter has already been discussed on our forum.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. probable; expected to happen or to be true
(2) adj. (of a person or thing) seeming suitable for a purpose; promising to be good or successful
(3) adv. (usually with 'most', 'very', 'quite') probably
(4) adj. expected to do a particular thing

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 有出息的，有前途的（指人，常搭配 young / lad）
uncommonMeanings.example: The old blacksmith eyed the ragged boy sweeping his floor and muttered, 'A likely lad, that one — sharp eyes, quick hands. He'll amount to something one day.' （读后续写·人物赏识·伏笔）

posExamples.sentence: As the first drops of rain spattered against the window, Grandma glanced at the darkening sky and sighed, 'It's likely to pour before nightfall — best we bring the washing in.' （读后续写·环境预兆·生活场景）
I am writing to remind all members that the sudden change in weather makes a downpour highly likely this weekend, so please bring raincoats and non-slip shoes for the hiking activity. （应用文·通知）
Students who read widely and reflect deeply are far more likely to develop independent judgement than those who passively memorise textbook answers. （议论文·阅读的价值）
Had she not hesitated at that crucial moment, she would most likely have caught the last train home and spared herself a night of wandering the empty platform. （读后续写·遗憾·虚拟语气）

idioms.example: 'The dog ate my entire essay?' the teacher repeated, one eyebrow raised. 'A likely story, John. I'll expect it on my desk by tomorrow morning.' （读后续写·师生对话·反讽）

collocations.example: A well-rested mind is far more likely to solve problems creatively than one worn down by endless late-night cramming. （议论文·作息与效率）
It is likely that the matter has already been discussed on our forum, so I would suggest searching the archives before posting a new question. （应用文·论坛回复）
The applicant with genuine volunteering experience is most likely to be chosen, for our committee values action over empty promises. （应用文·选拔说明）
Given her flawless rehearsals, it seemed highly likely that Mia would take home the first prize — yet fate, as it often does, had other plans. （读后续写·反转铺垫）
'Will you apologise to him first?' her friend asked. 'Not likely,' Anna snapped, folding her arms and turning away. （读后续写·倔强性格·对话）
Before rushing to conclusions, the young detective weighed every likely cause of the missing key, from a careless maid to a cunning intruder. （读后续写·推理）
The abandoned lighthouse struck them as a likely place to shelter from the raging storm. （读后续写·探险）
In all likelihood, the students' declining focus stems not from laziness but from the constant lure of their smartphones. （议论文·分心根源）

synonyms.example: The most probable explanation for his silence was not indifference, but a wound too deep to put into words. （读后续写·心理揣测）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：probable 较正式书面，多用于 it is probable that 结构，客观陈述可能性；likely 更口语通用，且可接 to do 结构，续写和对话都适用。

synonyms.example: Teenagers who sleep too little are prone to mood swings and lapses in concentration. （议论文·健康）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：prone 专指易发生不好的事（prone to error / to illness），带消极色彩；likely 中性，好坏皆可。

synonyms.example: Left unsupervised, young readers are apt to skim rather than savour a great novel. （议论文·阅读习惯）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：apt to do 强调习惯性、本性使然的倾向；likely to do 单纯陈述某次发生的概率。

advancedExpressions.expression: what had once seemed most likely now looked utterly impossible
advancedExpressions.example: What had once seemed the most likely ending — a triumphant homecoming — now looked utterly impossible as the floodwaters rose. （对比+反转，为续写高潮蓄势）

advancedExpressions.expression: you are likely to find that ...
advancedExpressions.example: Should you set aside just twenty minutes a day for reading, you are likely to find that a whole new world quietly opens before you. （虚拟 Should 倒装 + you are likely to 缓和语气，委婉给建议）

advancedExpressions.expression: those who ... are far more likely to ... than those who ...
advancedExpressions.example: Those who embrace failure as a teacher are far more likely to reach true excellence than those who flee from every mistake. （than 对比结构 + far 修饰强化，论证鲜明对立）

sentenceUpgrade.original: It might rain, so she went home early.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Sensing that a storm was likely to break at any moment, she quickened her pace, casting an anxious glance at the swollen clouds massing on the horizon. （读后续写·环境+心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 现在分词状语 Sensing that...前置揭示动机 + be likely to 表预感 + 环境描写(swollen clouds massing)烘托紧张氛围。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Students who read more will probably learn better.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm belief that students who immerse themselves in reading are far more likely to cultivate both eloquence and empathy than those who confine themselves to textbooks alone. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm belief that 表态主句 + are more likely to...than 对比结构 + 名词并列(eloquence and empathy)提升论证厚度。

translation: 独一无二的；独特的；独具的，特有的
sub_section: B2 对话填空
original_sentence: Everyone is unique.
readingExamples: Everyone is unique.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else
(2) adj. particularly remarkable, special, or unusual
(3) adj. (unique to sb/sth) belonging to or connected with only one particular person, place, or thing
(4) n. (formal, rare) a thing that is the only one of its kind

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （unique to）某地/某人特有的、专属的
uncommonMeanings.example: The haunting melody was unique to that remote mountain village — a song passed from grandmother to granddaughter, sung nowhere else on earth. （读后续写·文化传承·乡愁）

posExamples.sentence: The moment she unwrapped the gift, her breath caught: it was a unique hand-carved music box, its lid inlaid with mother-of-pearl that shimmered like frost under the lamplight. （读后续写·礼物·惊喜）
I am writing to invite you to our Cultural Festival, where you will enjoy a unique opportunity to experience calligraphy, paper-cutting and other treasures of Chinese tradition. （应用文·邀请信）
Every human being is unique, and it is precisely this diversity of talent and perspective that drives a society forward rather than dragging it into dull uniformity. （议论文·个性与多元）
As I stepped into the old workshop, the unique scent of sawdust and varnish carried me back to the summers I had spent watching Grandpa shape wood with patient, weathered hands. （读后续写·感官记忆·怀旧）

collocations.translation: 难得的、绝无仅有的机会
collocations.example: Volunteering abroad offers young people a unique opportunity to step outside their comfort zone and see the world through new eyes. （应用文·志愿招募）
The gentle warmth in her smile was unique to her, something no photograph could ever fully capture. （读后续写·人物刻画）
That night beneath the meteor shower remained a unique experience, one I would treasure long after the last star had faded. （读后续写·难忘经历）
Each dialect carries a unique feature that reflects the history and soul of the people who speak it. （议论文·语言文化）

collocations.translation: 个人独特的风格 / 声音
collocations.example: Rather than imitating famous authors, she gradually found her own unique voice, raw and unmistakably her own. （读后续写·成长）

collocations.translation: 唯一恰当地胜任 / 适合
collocations.example: Having grown up bilingual, Lily was uniquely qualified to bridge the two cultures during the exchange programme. （应用文·推荐信）
The old town charms visitors with a unique blend of ancient temples and bustling modern cafés. （应用文·景点介绍）
It is not perfection but her small imperfections that make her performance unique and deeply human. （议论文·艺术）

synonyms.example: His distinctive laugh echoed down the corridor, and everyone knew at once that Uncle Tom had arrived. （读后续写·人物出场）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：distinctive 强调特征鲜明、易于辨认（但可有多个同类）；unique 强调独一无二、绝无第二个。

synonyms.example: Her exceptional dedication earned her the respect of every teacher in the school. （应用文·表彰）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：exceptional 侧重程度上远超一般水平（优秀）；unique 侧重种类上的独一无二，未必含优劣评价。

synonyms.translation: 无与伦比的，无可比拟的
synonyms.example: The view from the summit was of unparalleled beauty, silencing even the most talkative of us. （读后续写·登顶）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：unparalleled 极正式，强调好到无人能及，多用于书面赞叹；unique 中性通用，日常与书面皆可。

advancedExpressions.expression: there was something unique about ..., something that ...
advancedExpressions.example: There was something unique about that battered old violin, something that made every note tremble with a lifetime of untold stories. （something...that 后置定语 + 拟人 tremble，赋予物品灵魂）

advancedExpressions.expression: this is a unique opportunity to ...
advancedExpressions.example: This is truly a unique opportunity to immerse yourself in a culture unlike any other, and I would hate for you to miss it. （倒装强调 + I would hate for you to miss 委婉催促）

advancedExpressions.expression: precisely because each of us is unique, ...
advancedExpressions.example: Precisely because each of us is unique, a wise society learns to celebrate difference rather than sand every individual down to the same dull shape. （precisely because 强调因果 + 比喻 sand down 生动批判）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The gift was special and I liked it very much.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The gift was unlike anything I had ever received — a unique, hand-stitched scarf into which, I later learned, my grandmother had woven strands of her own silver hair. （读后续写·情感）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 破折号补充信息 + unique 前置 + into which 定语从句揭示深意 + 细节(silver hair)催泪。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Everyone is different, and that is a good thing.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Every human being is unique, and it is this very uniqueness — not our sameness — that weaves the rich tapestry of human civilisation. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: it is...that 强调句 + 破折号插入对比(not our sameness) + 隐喻 tapestry 升华主旨。

sub_section: B2 对话填空
original_sentence: Don't take a passive role in the relationship.
readingExamples: Don't take a passive role in the relationship.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. accepting what happens or what people do without trying to change anything or oppose them
(2) adj. not participating readily or actively; inactive
(3) adj. (grammar) relating to the form of a verb in which the subject is affected by the action
(4) n. (grammar) the passive form of a verb

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （语法）被动语态
uncommonMeanings.example: In her essay, she overused the passive, and the teacher gently noted in the margin that active verbs would give her writing far more punch. （读后续写·写作指导）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （passive smoking）二手烟的，被动吸入的
uncommonMeanings.example: The campaign warned parents that passive smoking poses a serious threat to a child's developing lungs. （应用文·公益宣传）

posExamples.sentence: For years Emma had drifted through life in a passive daze, letting others decide her path — until the day she finally stood up, looked her father in the eye, and said, 'This time, I choose.' （读后续写·觉醒·转折）
I would like to suggest that we adopt a more active, rather than passive, approach to environmental protection, beginning with a weekly clean-up around our campus. （应用文·建议信）
A passive attitude towards learning — merely absorbing what teachers say without question — breeds dependence, whereas active inquiry cultivates the critical minds our era demands. （议论文·学习态度）
Don't take a passive role in the friendship, Teresa; a bond that only one person struggles to keep alive will wither like a flower left unwatered. （读后续写·劝慰·比喻）

collocations.example: Instead of taking a passive role in class, Tom began raising his hand, and his confidence grew with every question he dared to ask. （读后续写·转变）
A passive attitude towards one's own future is, in truth, a quiet surrender to circumstance. （议论文·人生态度）
Studies reveal that passive smoking harms non-smokers almost as much as the habit harms smokers themselves. （议论文·健康）
As the argument escalated, he could no longer remain passive, and stepped forward to defend his trembling classmate. （读后续写·挺身而出）
Through passive resistance rather than open conflict, the villagers quietly refused to abandon their ancestral land. （议论文·历史/抗争）
True progress has never sprung from the passive acceptance of the way things are, but from the courage to imagine how they might be. （议论文·变革）
The teacher explained that the passive voice can shift the reader's focus from the doer to the deed. （应用文·课堂讲解）
Passive learning fills the memory but rarely awakens the mind. （议论文·教育）

synonyms.example: For too long she had worn a submissive smile, swallowing every unfair word — but that smile, at last, began to fade. （读后续写·压抑与觉醒）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：submissive 强调对权威/他人意志的顺从屈服，程度更重；passive 泛指不主动、不反抗的消极状态。

synonyms.example: The volunteer group had grown inactive over the summer, and it fell to Lucy to breathe new life into it. （应用文·社团）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：inactive 客观描述缺乏活动/动作；passive 侧重面对外界不作反应、任其发生的心理姿态。

synonyms.example: How can we remain indifferent when our own river turns black with pollution? （议论文·环保呼吁）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：indifferent 强调情感上的冷漠不在乎；passive 强调行为上的不主动、不参与，未必冷漠。

advancedExpressions.expression: no longer the passive ... she had once been
advancedExpressions.example: She was no longer the passive, timid girl she had once been; something inside her had hardened into quiet, unbreakable resolve. （no longer...she had once been 对比今昔 + 分号并列刻画蜕变）

advancedExpressions.expression: rather than remaining passive, let us ...
advancedExpressions.example: Rather than remaining passive bystanders, let us roll up our sleeves and become the very change our community so badly needs. （rather than remaining passive 对比 + let us 号召 + 习语 roll up our sleeves 增色）

advancedExpressions.expression: passivity is not neutrality; it is a silent form of consent
advancedExpressions.example: Passivity is not neutrality; in the face of injustice, it is a silent form of consent. （警句式判断句 + 分号递进，观点犀利有力）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She used to be shy and did nothing, but then she changed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Where once she had stood on the sidelines, passive and voiceless, she now strode to the very front of the crowd, her chin lifted and her heart pounding with a courage she never knew she owned. （读后续写·蜕变）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Where once...she now 今昔对照结构 + 形容词并列(passive and voiceless) + 身体语言(chin lifted, heart pounding)外化心理。

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not just accept problems; we should act.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is high time we cast off our passive acceptance of these problems and took decisive action, for history rewards not the onlooker but the doer. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is high time (that) + 过去式虚拟 表紧迫呼吁 + not...but 对比(onlooker/doer)收束有力。

sub_section: B2 对话填空
original_sentence: Right now, it's just making you anxious and having a bad influence on your performance.
readingExamples: Right now, it's just making you anxious and having a bad influence on your performance.
definitionEn:
(1) n. how well or badly a person, machine, or organization does a piece of work or an activity
(2) n. the act of performing a play, concert, or some other form of entertainment
(3) n. the act of doing something, such as a job or task
(4) n. (informal) an act of behaving in a way that attracts attention, often a display of excessive fuss

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （口语）小题大做，一场闹剧，繁琐的过程
uncommonMeanings.example: Getting the stubborn old car to start on a frosty morning was such a performance that by the time the engine coughed to life, we were already late. （读后续写·生活趣事·夸张）

posExamples.sentence: As the final note of her performance faded into silence, the entire hall rose to its feet, and Mia — trembling, tearful, disbelieving — realized that all those lonely hours of practice had not been in vain. （读后续写·舞台·圆梦）
I am writing to invite you to our school's charity performance next Friday, where students will stage songs, dances and short plays to raise funds for children in mountain areas. （应用文·邀请信）
Judging students solely by their academic performance is like measuring a fish by its ability to climb a tree — it blinds us to the countless other talents that make each learner shine. （议论文·教育评价·比喻）
Right now, all that pressure is just making you anxious and having a bad influence on your performance, so let's step back, breathe, and take things one small step at a time. （读后续写·安慰·对话）

collocations.example: The shy boy gave a performance so moving that even the strictest judge wiped away a tear. （读后续写·惊艳表演）
Regular exercise and adequate sleep can markedly boost a student's academic performance. （议论文·健康与学业）
Her academic performance soared once she stopped comparing herself with others and started competing only with her past self. （读后续写·心态转变）

collocations.phrase: have an influence / effect on one's performance
collocations.example: Constant anxiety, the coach warned, could have a devastating effect on an athlete's performance on the day that mattered most. （读后续写·比赛前）
Nothing compares to the electric thrill of a live performance, where every mistake and every triumph unfolds before your eyes. （应用文·活动感想）

collocations.phrase: under pressure of performance / performance anxiety
collocations.translation: 表演压力 / 表现焦虑
collocations.example: Performance anxiety had gripped her so tightly that her fingers froze above the piano keys. （读后续写·怯场）

collocations.translation: 在表演中 / 巅峰状态
collocations.example: To reach peak performance, an athlete must train not only the body but also the mind. （议论文·竞技）

collocations.phrase: a standing ovation for one's performance
collocations.example: The audience gave a standing ovation for a performance that had, quite literally, taken their breath away. （读后续写·高潮）

synonyms.example: Winning the national contest was the crowning achievement of years of quiet, stubborn effort. （读后续写·成就时刻）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：achievement 强调努力换来的成果、成就，含褒义结果；performance 中性，指做事的表现或过程，好坏皆可。

synonyms.example: The talent show drew half the town, its little stage ablaze with light and laughter. （应用文·活动报道）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：show 口语常用，泛指娱乐性演出/展示；performance 更正式，也可指个人在任务/考试中的表现。

synonyms.example: Her confident presentation on plastic pollution won the class over within minutes. （应用文·课堂展示）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：presentation 特指有条理的讲解/演示（如报告、汇报）；performance 泛指表演或整体表现。

advancedExpressions.expression: the performance of a lifetime
advancedExpressions.example: In that trembling, tear-streaked moment, she knew she had just given the performance of a lifetime — not because it was flawless, but because it was fearless. （the...of a lifetime 最高级式表达 + not because...but because 揭示深意）

advancedExpressions.expression: you are cordially invited to witness a performance that ...
advancedExpressions.example: You are cordially invited to witness a performance that promises to warm your heart and remind us all what a little kindness can achieve. （cordially invited 正式邀请套语 + that 定语从句渲染亮点）

advancedExpressions.expression: to reduce a person to a single performance is to ...
advancedExpressions.example: To reduce a person to a single number on a performance report is to overlook the vast, uncharted continent of human potential. （To do...is to do 对称判断句 + 隐喻 uncharted continent 批判单一评价）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She performed well and everyone clapped.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: As the last note of her performance dissolved into a breathless hush, the hall erupted — a thunder of applause washing over her like a warm, unstoppable tide. （读后续写·舞台高潮）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: As 时间状语从句铺垫 + 破折号引出爆发 + 比喻(thunder of applause / warm tide)双重渲染感染力。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Pressure can make students do worse in exams.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Excessive pressure, far from sharpening a student's edge, often erodes both confidence and concentration, thereby dragging down the very performance it was meant to improve. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 插入语 far from doing 让步 + thereby 引出结果 + the very...it was meant to 强调结构，凸显讽刺与因果。

sub_section: B2 对话填空
original_sentence: Jack: Cheer up, Teresa.
readingExamples: Jack: Cheer up, Teresa.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. v. to become happier, or to make someone feel happier, especially when they have been sad or worried
(2) phr. v. to make a place look brighter or more attractive
(3) phr. v. (imperative) an encouraging way of telling someone not to be sad

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使（某地/某物）变得明亮、活泼、有生气
uncommonMeanings.example: A single vase of sunflowers on the sill was enough to cheer up the whole dim little kitchen. （读后续写·家的温暖·环境）

posExamples.sentence: Seeing his sister slumped over her desk in tears, Jack knelt beside her, ruffled her hair and whispered, 'Cheer up, Teresa — the world always looks brighter after a good cry and a bar of chocolate.' （读后续写·兄妹·安慰）
To cheer up the elderly residents at the nursing home, our club will bring homemade cards, warm blankets and an afternoon of familiar old songs. （应用文·志愿活动方案）
Rather than dwelling endlessly on our failures, we should learn to cheer up, dust ourselves off, and turn each setback into the first step of a fresh climb. （议论文·逆境心态）
Her spirits cheered up the moment the acceptance letter slipped through the door, and for the first time in weeks the whole house seemed to breathe again. （读后续写·喜讯·氛围转变）

idioms.translation: 振作点！打起精神来！（口语鼓励）
idioms.example: 'Cheer up! It's not the end of the world,' Mum said softly, pressing a warm cup of cocoa into my frozen hands. （读后续写·母女·安慰对话）

idioms.idiom: cheer up, things could be worse
idioms.translation: 打起精神，情况本可能更糟
idioms.example: Cheer up, things could be worse — at least we still have each other and a roof over our heads. （读后续写·患难与共）

collocations.example: Nothing could cheer him up after the loss — until his old dog limped into the room and rested its head on his knee. （读后续写·治愈）
'Cheer up!' the coach barked, clapping the boy on the shoulder. 'A champion is just someone who refused to quit.' （读后续写·激励）
To cheer herself up on the gloomy afternoon, she baked a batch of cookies and filled the flat with their sweet, comforting smell. （读后续写·自我疗愈）
A fresh coat of yellow paint did wonders to cheer up the drab old classroom. （应用文·班级美化）

collocations.phrase: do sth to cheer sb up
collocations.example: The whole class secretly planned a surprise party to cheer up their homesick exchange student. （读后续写·友情）
No matter how hard we tried to cheer him up, Grandpa's gaze kept drifting to the empty chair by the window. （读后续写·思念·细节）

synonyms.example: She wrapped her arms around her sobbing friend, whispering words of comfort until the trembling slowly stilled. （读后续写·安慰）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：comfort 侧重减轻痛苦、给予慰藉，常针对悲伤/受伤者；cheer up 侧重从低落中变得开心振作，更口语、更轻快。

synonyms.example: A single word of praise from the teacher was enough to encourage the timid boy to try again. （读后续写·激励）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：encourage 侧重给人勇气与动力去行动；cheer up 侧重使情绪由悲转喜，未必促成行动。

synonyms.example: The first birdsong of spring never failed to lift her spirits, however heavy her heart had been. （读后续写·希望）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：lift one's spirits 为地道书面表达，强调心情被提振，文采更足；cheer up 更口语、更常用于祈使鼓励。

advancedExpressions.expression: 'Cheer up,' sb said, ... — words that ...
advancedExpressions.example: 'Cheer up,' he said, pressing a crumpled tissue into her hand — three small words that, somehow, held back the flood of her tears. （对话 + 破折号引出细节 + three small words 回指点睛）

advancedExpressions.expression: we hope this small gesture will cheer you up
advancedExpressions.example: We hope this small gesture will cheer you up during your recovery, and remind you that the whole class is cheering you on. （we hope...will 温情祝愿 + cheer up / cheer on 双关呼应）

advancedExpressions.expression: the ability to cheer oneself up is ...
advancedExpressions.example: The ability to cheer oneself up in the darkest hour is not naivety but a quiet, hard-won form of courage. （抽象名词化主语 + not...but 重新定义，提升思辨高度）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He tried to make her happy, so he told a joke.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Desperate to cheer her up, Jack pulled the silliest face he could muster, and at last — reluctantly, then helplessly — a smile broke through the clouds of her grief. （读后续写·兄妹温情）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 形容词短语 Desperate to...前置表动机 + 破折号副词递进(reluctantly, then helplessly) + 比喻 clouds of grief 描摹心理。

sentenceUpgrade.original: When we are sad, we should try to feel better.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When life presses us down, the wisest thing we can do is not to wallow in sorrow but to cheer ourselves up, square our shoulders, and face the next dawn with hope. （议论文·励志）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: When 状语从句起势 + not to...but to 对比结构 + 三动词并列(cheer, square, face)推动语势。

translation: 催促，逼迫；按，压；挤，推；报章杂志，报刊；新闻工作者，新闻界
sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: When we're at home, she keeps pressing me to study all the time.
readingExamples: When we're at home, she keeps pressing me to study all the time.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to push something firmly, often with your finger, or to push something against a surface
(2) v. to try hard to persuade someone to do something, or to urge them strongly
(3) v. to make clothes smooth using an iron
(4) n. newspapers and magazines, and the journalists who work for them (the press)
(5) n. a machine used for printing, or for pressing or crushing things

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 报刊界，新闻界；新闻媒体（the press）
uncommonMeanings.example: By dawn the story had reached the national press, and reporters were already gathering, cameras poised, outside the small-town hospital. （读后续写·意外走红·媒体）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 印刷机；出版社（university press）
uncommonMeanings.example: The ancient printing press, silent for decades, groaned back to life as the old craftsman fed the first sheet between its heavy rollers. （读后续写·旧技艺·工坊）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 熨烫（衣物）
uncommonMeanings.example: The night before the interview, she pressed her father's old shirt with trembling care, smoothing out every crease as if smoothing out her own fear. （读后续写·细节·紧张）

posExamples.sentence: When we're at home, she keeps pressing me to study all the time, and the harder she pushes, the more the words on the page seem to blur before my tired eyes. （读后续写·亲子压力·心理）
With shaking hands he pressed the emergency button and shouted for help, his voice cracking as the smoke curled thicker around the stairwell. （读后续写·危急时刻·动作）
I am writing to invite members of the press to attend our school's charity gala, so that the story of our students' generosity may reach and inspire the wider community. （应用文·邀请信）
Parents who constantly press their children to excel may, however well-meaning, end up crushing the very curiosity that makes true learning possible. （议论文·家庭教育）

idioms.example: Though exhausted and blistered, the climbers pressed on, for the summit — and their long-held dream — lay only a few hundred metres above. （读后续写·坚持·登山）

idioms.translation: 时间/金钱紧张，捉襟见肘
idioms.example: Pressed for time, she scribbled a hasty note, grabbed her bag, and dashed for the door without so much as a backward glance. （读后续写·匆忙）
Sensing his friend's discomfort, he chose not to press the point, and let the awkward silence gently dissolve. （读后续写·体贴）

collocations.example: However gently his mother pressed him to speak, the boy only lowered his eyes and clutched the letter tighter. （读后续写·沉默·内心）
She pressed the button, held her breath, and watched the lift doors slide shut on the life she was leaving behind. （读后续写·离别·转折）
The students pressed for a longer library opening time, arguing that quiet study space was scarce during exam season. （应用文·倡议）
The freedom of the press, the editor argued, is the watchful eye that keeps power honest. （议论文·媒体角色）
At the press conference, the young inventor's hands trembled, but her voice rang clear and steady. （读后续写·公众场合）
He pressed his ear against the cold door, straining to catch the faint whisper of footsteps beyond. （读后续写·悬疑·动作）
She pressed her lips together and blinked hard, refusing to let a single tear betray how much the words had hurt. （读后续写·隐忍·神态）
Under the press of the looming deadline, the team worked through the night, fuelled by cold coffee and sheer determination. （读后续写·奋战）

collocations.translation: 乘胜追击；着力强调（观点）
collocations.example: The debater pressed home her message with a torrent of facts that left her opponent grasping for words. （议论文·辩论）

synonyms.example: 'Go now, while you still can,' the old man urged, his frail hand pushing me gently but firmly towards the open door. （读后续写·催促·别离）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：urge 侧重恳切地劝说、力劝（含善意期盼）；press 语气更硬，含施压、逼迫之意，甚至令人厌烦。

synonyms.example: His coach pushed him harder than anyone, and years later he would be grateful for every unforgiving drill. （读后续写·严师）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：push 与 press 都可表逼迫，push 更口语、范围更广（推动/督促）；press 常搭 press sb to do，强调持续施压。

synonyms.example: She squeezed his hand once, hard, then let go and stepped onto the departing train. （读后续写·离别·动作）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析：squeeze 强调用力挤压/攥紧（多为具体动作）；press 指按压、施压，动作与抽象义（催逼）皆可。

advancedExpressions.expression: the more sb pressed ..., the more ...
advancedExpressions.example: The more his father pressed him to choose a 'safe' career, the more fiercely his heart clung to the paintbrush he loved. （the more...the more 递进结构 + 内心对抗，凸显叛逆与坚持）

advancedExpressions.expression: we press for immediate action on ...
advancedExpressions.example: On behalf of all students, we press for immediate action on the crumbling sports facilities before an accident forces our hand. （On behalf of 正式立场 + press for 敦促 + before 从句渲染紧迫）

advancedExpressions.expression: there is a fine line between pressing sb and crushing sb
advancedExpressions.example: There is a fine line between pressing a child towards excellence and crushing the joy of learning altogether; wise parents learn exactly where it lies. （there is a fine line between...and 辩证句式 + 分号补足观点，思辨精准）

sentenceUpgrade.original: My mother always tells me to study, and it makes me stressed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When we're at home, she keeps pressing me to study every waking hour, until the endless reminders coil around my chest like a tightening rope, squeezing the very love of learning out of me. （读后续写·亲子压力）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: keeps pressing me 持续压迫 + until 引出结果 + 明喻(coil like a tightening rope) + squeeze...out of 呼应压迫主题。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Parents should not force children too much to do well.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: While a measure of encouragement is undoubtedly valuable, parents who relentlessly press their children to excel risk extinguishing the inner spark upon which all genuine achievement ultimately depends. （议论文·正式）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: While 让步从句平衡观点 + relentlessly 副词强化 + risk doing 表隐患 + 比喻(inner spark)与 upon which 定语从句升华论证。

sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: I'm eager for my parents' love.
readingExamples: I'm eager for my parents' love.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. wanting to do or have something very much, and showing this in the way you behave
(2) adj. showing keen interest, enthusiasm or impatience
(3) adj. (eager for / eager to do sth) strongly wishing to obtain or experience something

posExamples.sentence: The moment the bell rang, a dozen eager faces pressed against the classroom window, their eyes shining as the first snow of the year drifted silently onto the playground. （读后续写·校园·期待）
I am writing to apply for the position of volunteer guide, for I am eager to contribute my energy to promoting our city's rich culture to foreign visitors. （应用文·申请信）
Young people today are increasingly eager to prove their worth, yet true growth demands not restless ambition but the patience to master one skill at a time. （议论文·青年成长）
Trembling with cold and fear, the stray puppy nonetheless wagged its tail, its eager eyes begging the boy for a scrap of warmth and companionship. （读后续写·人与动物·温情）

collocations.example: Having been apart for three long years, the two brothers were eager for a reunion that seemed almost too good to be true. （读后续写·亲情·团聚）
The new intern was eager to make a good impression, so she arrived at the office a full hour before anyone else. （读后续写·职场·奋斗）
As an eager learner, Tom never let a single question go unanswered, staying behind after class until the teacher had explained every detail. （读后续写·师生·勤奋）
The children waited in eager anticipation, counting down the seconds until the fireworks would light up the winter sky. （读后续写·节日·期盼）
An eager crowd gathered outside the newly opened library, each person hoping to be among the first to borrow a book. （应用文·新闻报道）

collocations.translation: 工作卖力的人;过分热心的人
collocations.example: Always the eager beaver, Lily signed up for every committee, determined to leave her mark on the school before graduation. （读后续写·人物性格）

collocations.phrase: cast an eager glance / eye at
collocations.example: She cast an eager glance at the notice board, her heart pounding as she searched the list for her own name. （读后续写·揭晓·紧张）

collocations.translation: 急于讨好;一心想让人满意
collocations.example: The young waiter, eager to please, refilled our cups before they were even half empty. （读后续写·服务·细节）

synonyms.example: She was so keen on joining the debate club that she practised her arguments in front of the mirror every night. （读后续写·兴趣·执着）
synonyms.usage: 英式常用,常搭配 keen on doing / keen to do;与 eager 近似但语气略平实,更强调持续的兴趣爱好

synonyms.example: The volunteers gave the visitors an enthusiastic welcome, their warm smiles instantly putting everyone at ease. （应用文·活动报道）
synonyms.usage: 侧重外露的热情与积极态度,强调情绪的高涨;eager 更强调对某目标的向往和急切

synonyms.translation: 急切的,渴望的(此义中性偏急)
synonyms.example: He was anxious to explain himself before the misunderstanding grew any deeper. （读后续写·误会·澄清）
synonyms.usage: 作"急切想做"解时近于 eager,但常暗含焦虑不安;eager 则是积极正面的渴望

advancedExpressions.expression: so eager was sb. to do sth that ...
advancedExpressions.example: So eager was he to catch a glimpse of his idol that he squeezed through the crowd, heedless of the elbows jabbing at his ribs. （so + adj. 倒装强调,前置渴望之强烈,续写高潮段增强张力）

advancedExpressions.expression: I am eager to ..., which is why I am writing to ...
advancedExpressions.example: I am eager to broaden my horizons through cultural exchange, which is precisely why I am writing to apply for this exchange programme. （eager 开门见山表明动机,which 引导非限定从句自然衔接目的）

advancedExpressions.expression: far from being merely eager, sb. must also ...
advancedExpressions.example: Far from being merely eager for success, the young generation must also cultivate the resilience to endure repeated failure. （far from 让步转折,由"渴望"提升到"更需坚韧"的辩证论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: The boy was eager to open the gift.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The boy's fingers trembled with eager impatience as he tore at the wrapping paper, his heart drumming against his ribs at the thought of what lay hidden beneath. （读后续写·动作+心理描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 化"渴望"为具体动作(fingers trembled, tore at) + 心理外化(heart drumming) + at the thought of 引出期待的对象,画面感陡增

sentenceUpgrade.original: Students are eager to succeed.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is undeniable that today's students are eager to succeed; yet genuine achievement, I would argue, springs not from restless haste but from patient, deliberate effort. （议论文·辩证升级）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is undeniable that... 让步开篇 + 分号连接对立观点 + I would argue 插入语增强论证口吻 + not from...but from 平行对比点明主张

translation: 青年时期；青春；(the youth)年轻人
sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: Everyone says that youth is a time for adventure, but my parents disagree.
readingExamples: Everyone says that youth is a time for adventure, but my parents disagree.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the period of time when someone is young, especially the time before a child becomes an adult
(2) n. the quality or state of being young; the energy and freshness associated with being young
(3) n. a young man, typically a teenager or young adult
(4) n. (the youth) young people considered as a group

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 小伙子,青年男子(单数,常含轻微贬义或距离感)
uncommonMeanings.example: A hooded youth loitered at the corner of the alley, and the old shopkeeper instinctively drew the bolt across his door. （读后续写·街头·戒备氛围）

posExamples.sentence: In his youth, my grandfather had roamed the mountains barefoot, and even now, at eighty, his eyes still sparkled whenever he spoke of those carefree, sunlit days. （读后续写·怀旧·祖辈回忆）
On behalf of the student union, I sincerely invite the youth of our school to join the tree-planting campaign and devote their energy to a greener campus. （应用文·倡议书）
Youth is not merely a stage of life to be hurried through, but a precious window in which curiosity, courage and ideals should be nurtured for a lifetime. （议论文·青春的价值）
The gymnast moved with a grace and vigour that spoke of youth, yet her disciplined focus revealed a maturity far beyond her years. （读后续写·人物·矛盾特质）

idioms.idiom: in the flower / bloom of one's youth
idioms.example: Cut down in the bloom of his youth, the young pilot became a symbol of sacrifice that the whole nation would remember. （读后续写·纪念·崇高）

idioms.translation: 青春之泉(永葆青春的源泉)
idioms.example: She laughed that gardening was her fountain of youth, keeping both her hands busy and her heart forever young. （读后续写·晚年·豁达）

collocations.example: In her youth, my mother had dreamed of becoming a pianist, and now those unfinished dreams live on in the songs she hums while cooking. （读后续写·母亲·遗憾与传承）

collocations.phrase: the youth of today / today's youth
collocations.example: The youth of today shoulder a responsibility no less weighty than that of any generation before them. （议论文·青年责任）
He deeply regretted having wasted his youth on trivial pleasures instead of pursuing a craft that could have defined his life. （读后续写·悔悟）
With all the energy of youth, the volunteers cleared the flooded street in a single afternoon. （应用文·活动报道）
Time spares neither youth nor beauty, but it can never erase the wisdom a person earns along the way. （议论文·时间与成长）

collocations.translation: 青年中心 / 青年旅舍
collocations.example: The newly built youth centre offers free reading rooms and workshops where teenagers can spend their weekends meaningfully. （应用文·通知）
From youth to old age, he remained loyal to the small village school where he had first learned to read. （读后续写·坚守·一生）

synonyms.example: Adolescence is a turbulent bridge between childhood and adulthood, when the soul searches restlessly for its own shape. （议论文·成长阶段）
synonyms.usage: 特指从儿童到成人的过渡期(约13-19岁),更学术、更强调身心变化;youth 泛指年轻阶段,范围更广

synonyms.example: As a teenager, she filled countless notebooks with poems she was too shy to show anyone. （读后续写·少女·内向）
synonyms.usage: 具体指十几岁的人,口语常用;youth 可指人也可指时期,更书面、更文学化

synonyms.example: The line between youth and adult is drawn not by age alone but by the readiness to take responsibility. （议论文·成长界定）
synonyms.usage: 作对照概念时反衬 youth,强调成熟与责任;写作中常与 youth 并列构成对比

advancedExpressions.expression: the sb. of his youth had ..., but now ...
advancedExpressions.example: The carefree boy of his youth had vanished; in his place stood a man weathered by years, yet strangely at peace. （名词短语 the...of his youth 凝练往昔 + but now 时空对照,续写人物弧光）

advancedExpressions.expression: as the youth of a new era, we ought to ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the youth of a new era, we ought to shoulder our responsibilities and devote our talents to the service of society. （身份定位开篇 + ought to 义务情态,增强号召力）

advancedExpressions.expression: youth lies not in ... but in ...
advancedExpressions.example: Youth lies not in the smoothness of one's face but in the vigour of one's spirit and the boldness of one's dreams. （lies not in...but in 抽象定义句式,由外在转向内在,升华主旨）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He remembered his youth happily.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Whenever the scent of osmanthus drifted through the autumn air, he was carried back to his youth — to barefoot races down the hillside and laughter that echoed until dusk swallowed the light. （读后续写·感官触发回忆）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 气味触发记忆(scent of osmanthus) + 破折号引出具体画面 + 平行意象(races, laughter) + 拟人(dusk swallowed the light),营造怀旧氛围

sentenceUpgrade.original: Young people should work hard.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is my firm conviction that the youth of our nation should not squander these irreplaceable years, but rather channel their boundless energy into pursuits that will enrich both themselves and the world. （议论文·正式倡议）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is my firm conviction that... 正式主句 + not...but rather 转折递进 + channel...into 隐喻用法 + 双宾并列(themselves and the world)升华格局

sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: Everyone says that youth is a time for adventure, but my parents disagree.
readingExamples: Everyone says that youth is a time for adventure, but my parents disagree.
definitionEn:
(1) n. an exciting experience in which dangerous or unusual things happen
(2) n. the excitement produced by new, dangerous or exotic experiences; a willingness to take risks
(3) n. an unusual, exciting or daring undertaking
(4) n. a commercial or financial venture involving risk

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 投机的商业冒险,风险事业(书面/旧义)
uncommonMeanings.example: The merchant sank his entire fortune into a single trading adventure to the East, gambling everything on winds he could not control. （读后续写·大航海·孤注一掷）

posExamples.sentence: The narrow mountain trail, the sudden storm, the shelter found by sheer luck — that unforgettable night turned an ordinary hike into the greatest adventure of my life. （读后续写·徒步·意外）
I would like to invite you to join our summer expedition to the Gobi Desert, an adventure that promises breathtaking scenery and lifelong friendships. （应用文·邀请信）
Life without any sense of adventure would be a still pond; it is the courage to step into the unknown that gives our days their colour and depth. （议论文·冒险与人生）
For the shy new student, simply raising her hand in class felt like an adventure, each word a small leap across the chasm of her own fear. （读后续写·成长·突破自我）

collocations.example: It was her father's sense of adventure that first taught her to see every closed door as an invitation rather than an obstacle. （读后续写·父女·传承）

collocations.phrase: seek / go in search of adventure
collocations.example: Restless and full of dreams, the young sailor left his quiet fishing village to seek adventure on the open sea. （读后续写·启程·追梦）

collocations.phrase: set off / embark on an adventure
collocations.example: At dawn, backpacks slung over their shoulders, the three friends embarked on an adventure that none of them would ever forget. （读后续写·出发·激动）
A spirit of adventure, tempered by careful preparation, is what separates a reckless wanderer from a true explorer. （议论文·冒险的分寸）
"We had quite an adventure getting here," she laughed, brushing the mud from her boots and the leaves from her hair. （读后续写·对话·历险后）

collocations.translation: 冒险故事 / 小说 / 电影
collocations.example: As a boy he devoured adventure stories by torchlight under the blanket, long after his mother had turned off the lights. （读后续写·童年·痴迷阅读）
Nothing could quench his thirst for adventure — not warnings, not weather, not the tears of those who loved him. （读后续写·执着·冒险者）
The exchange programme offered us the adventure of a lifetime, plunging us into a culture utterly different from our own. （应用文·感想）

synonyms.example: The scientific expedition to the polar region lasted six gruelling months and rewrote the textbooks on climate change. （议论文·科考·意义）
synonyms.usage: 指有明确目的、有组织的探险或考察,常涉科研或征服;adventure 更泛指一般的刺激经历,不必有正式目标

synonyms.example: Starting a business straight out of school was a bold venture, but she was determined to prove the doubters wrong. （读后续写·创业·决心）
synonyms.usage: 多指商业或有风险的尝试,强调可能失败的投入;adventure 更偏重刺激与经历本身的乐趣

synonyms.example: His quest for the lost manuscript took him across three continents and into the dustiest corners of forgotten libraries. （读后续写·追寻·执着）
synonyms.usage: 强调为某一崇高或长期目标的持续追寻,带文学色彩;adventure 更侧重单次的、刺激的经历

advancedExpressions.expression: little did sb. know that ... would turn into an adventure
advancedExpressions.example: Little did they know that a simple detour to avoid the traffic would turn into the wildest adventure of their summer. （little did 倒装 + 埋伏笔,续写开篇预示情节反转）

advancedExpressions.expression: join us for an adventure that will ...
advancedExpressions.example: Join us for an adventure that will not only challenge your limits but also forge friendships to last a lifetime. （祈使句号召 + not only...but also 双重卖点,增强吸引力）

advancedExpressions.expression: adventure is not about ... but about ...
advancedExpressions.example: True adventure is not about escaping danger but about embracing uncertainty with an open and fearless heart. （not about...but about 重新定义 + 抽象名词化升华主旨）

sentenceUpgrade.original: They went on an exciting adventure.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: With their hearts pounding and the wind roaring in their ears, they plunged into an adventure that would test not only their strength but the very depths of their courage. （读后续写·动作+情感渲染）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: with 独立主格铺垫氛围(hearts pounding, wind roaring) + plunge into 动词强化投入感 + not only...but the very depths of 递进升华内涵

sentenceUpgrade.original: Adventure makes life interesting.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It is precisely the willingness to embrace adventure — to venture beyond the comfortable and the familiar — that transforms a life of mere existence into one of genuine meaning. （议论文·强调句升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It is...that 强调句突出核心 + 破折号插入解释(venture beyond...) + transform...into 对比句式(existence vs. meaning)拔高立意

word: be on sb's back about sth
sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: ' They're always on my back about something.
readingExamples: ' They're always on my back about something.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. to keep criticizing, nagging or pressuring someone about something in a way that annoys them
(2) phr. to repeatedly urge or remind someone to do something, often causing irritation

posExamples.sentence: My coach had been on my back about my sloppy footwork for weeks, but the day I finally nailed the routine, his stern face broke into the widest grin I had ever seen. （读后续写·师徒·严厉背后的期望）
I understand that parents are constantly on their children's backs about grades because they love them, yet endless nagging often does more harm than good. （议论文·亲子沟通）
"Stop being on my back about it," she snapped, then instantly regretted the sharpness in her voice as she saw the hurt flicker across her mother's face. （读后续写·冲突·愧疚）

idioms.example: "Just get off my back and let me try it my own way for once," he pleaded, his voice cracking under the weight of everyone's expectations. （读后续写·压力·渴望自主）
Her condescending tone immediately got my back up, though I forced myself to stay polite. （读后续写·摩擦·隐忍）

collocations.translation: 总是缠着 / 数落某人
collocations.example: Feeling that his parents were always on his back, the boy began to dread coming home after school. （读后续写·家庭·压抑）

collocations.phrase: be on sb's back about the homework / grades
collocations.translation: 为作业 / 成绩缠磨某人
collocations.example: My teacher was on my back about the unfinished essay until, guilt-stricken, I stayed up all night to complete it. （读后续写·督促·转变）

collocations.translation: 持续督促 / 烦扰某人
collocations.example: She had to keep on her little brother's back about his piano practice, or he would abandon it for cartoons within minutes. （读后续写·姐弟·日常）

collocations.translation: 被某人缠着,被某人施压
collocations.example: With his boss on his back over the deadline, he could hardly concentrate on doing the job well. （读后续写·职场·压力）

synonyms.example: His grandmother nagged at him gently to wear a scarf, and only years later did he understand that nagging was her language of love. （读后续写·祖孙·亲情）
synonyms.usage: 指反复唠叨琐事使人厌烦,是 be on sb's back 最贴近的近义表达;nag 为动词,更书面通用

synonyms.example: The children pestered their father about the promised trip to the seaside until he finally gave in. （读后续写·孩童·央求）
synonyms.usage: 强调反复请求或打扰以求达到目的,常用于孩子缠大人;be on sb's back 更侧重批评施压

synonyms.translation: 不停地催促 / 唠叨某人
synonyms.example: My mother kept on at me to apply for the scholarship, and in the end her persistence paid off. （读后续写·母亲·坚持）
synonyms.usage: 英式口语,指持续不断地催促或劝说;与 be on sb's back 语气相近,但结果可正可负

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. had always been on my back about ..., and only then did I realize ...
advancedExpressions.example: My father had always been on my back about my carelessness, and only then, standing amid the wreckage of my mistake, did I realize how right he had been. （only then did 倒装 + 事后顿悟,续写情感升华）

advancedExpressions.expression: rather than constantly being on sb's back, it would be wiser to ...
advancedExpressions.example: Rather than constantly being on your child's back about every small failing, it would be far wiser to offer gentle encouragement and trust. （rather than...it would be wiser to 委婉建议句式,应用文劝导口吻）

advancedExpressions.expression: when parents are always on their children's backs, ... ; conversely, ...
advancedExpressions.example: When parents are always on their children's backs, they may breed rebellion rather than obedience; conversely, patient guidance often earns lasting respect. （对比句式 conversely 引出辩证,议论文两面论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: My parents are always on my back about studying.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Day after day my parents were on my back about my studies, their well-meant reminders gradually hardening into a wall between us that neither side knew how to climb. （读后续写·亲子隔阂·比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Day after day 时间状语强化持续感 + well-meant 让步点明善意 + harden into a wall 隐喻代际隔阂 + that 定语从句延展画面

sentenceUpgrade.original: It is not good to keep criticizing children.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Being perpetually on a child's back, however well-intentioned, tends to erode confidence rather than build it, for constant criticism whispers a quiet message: you are not enough. （议论文·因果论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 动名词作主语正式化 + however well-intentioned 插入让步 + erode...rather than build 对比动词 + for 引出原因 + 冒号后拟人化点明危害

sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: However, just as a baby kangaroo must learn to protect itself when it leaves its mother's pocket, I will have to learn to protect myself when I grow up.
readingExamples: However, just as a baby kangaroo must learn to protect itself when it leaves its mother's pocket, I will have to learn to protect myself when I grow up.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a large Australian mammal that moves by jumping on its powerful hind legs and carries its young in a pouch on the front of its body
(2) n. (kangaroo court) an informal, unofficial court that ignores standards of justice and law

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (kangaroo court)非法私设的法庭,不公正的裁决场合
uncommonMeanings.example: The whole hearing felt like a kangaroo court, its verdict decided long before the first witness had even spoken. （读后续写·蒙冤·不公）

posExamples.sentence: At the first light of dawn, a kangaroo bounded across the dusty road, its powerful hind legs propelling it over the fence in a single, breathtaking leap. （读后续写·澳洲·自然画面）
During our trip to Australia, we were thrilled to feed a gentle kangaroo by hand, an experience that made the whole class fall in love with wildlife. （应用文·游记 / 报道）
Just as a baby kangaroo must one day leave its mother's pouch, every young person must eventually step out of the shelter of family and learn to stand alone. （议论文·独立成长·比喻论证）

idioms.translation: 非法私设的法庭;不公正的审判
idioms.example: He refused to defend himself before what he rightly called a kangaroo court, where the outcome had been fixed from the start. （读后续写·正义·抗争）

collocations.example: Peeping out from its mother's pouch, the baby kangaroo blinked shyly at the visitors before ducking back into the warmth. （读后续写·动物·萌态）
A kangaroo's pouch is nature's cradle, sheltering the tiny joey until it is strong enough to face the world. （议论文·自然·保护）
As the sun dipped below the horizon, a mob of kangaroos grazed peacefully across the golden grassland. （读后续写·黄昏·宁静）
The excited puppy bounded like a kangaroo across the lawn, unable to contain its joy at seeing its owner. （读后续写·重逢·喜悦）
The reserve is home to hundreds of wild kangaroos, and visitors are urged to keep a respectful distance. （应用文·须知 / 告示）

advancedExpressions.expression: with each powerful leap, the kangaroo ...
advancedExpressions.example: With each powerful leap, the kangaroo seemed to defy gravity itself, sailing across the open plain as if the earth could scarcely hold it. （with 独立主格 + 拟人 defy gravity,续写自然动态描写）

advancedExpressions.expression: we should protect ... such as the kangaroo, before ...
advancedExpressions.example: We should act now to protect precious species such as the kangaroo, before human carelessness robs future generations of these living wonders. （祈使呼吁 + before 从句强化紧迫感,倡议书结尾）

advancedExpressions.expression: just as a kangaroo ..., so too must sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: Just as a kangaroo must trust its own legs once it leaves the pouch, so too must the young learn to rely on their own judgement once they leave home. （just as...so too 类比句式,以自然现象论证成长道理）

sentenceUpgrade.original: A kangaroo jumped across the field.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In one fluid, effortless bound, the kangaroo cleared the field and vanished into the shimmering heat, leaving only a trail of dust dancing in the morning light. （读后续写·动态+环境描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: in one...bound 强调动作干脆利落 + clear 精准动词表"跃过" + vanish into 营造消失感 + leaving 现在分词收尾定格画面(dust dancing)

sentenceUpgrade.original: A young kangaroo must leave its mother.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Nature offers no gentler teacher than necessity: just as the young kangaroo must one day abandon the safety of the pouch, so every fledgling soul must brave the wide, uncertain world alone. （议论文·哲理升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 冒号引出格言式主句 + just as...so 类比结构 + fledgling soul 隐喻年轻人 + brave 动词化"勇敢面对" + 形容词叠加(wide, uncertain)渲染世界之广

translation: 灵活的，可变动的；柔韧的
sub_section: Part A — 三位青少年的问题
original_sentence: I wish they could be more flexible so that I can make my own choices about what to do in my spare time.
readingExamples: I wish they could be more flexible so that I can make my own choices about what to do in my spare time.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. able to change or be changed easily according to the situation; adaptable
(2) adj. (of a person) willing to change plans or ideas in order to suit new conditions
(3) adj. (of a material or object) able to bend or be bent easily without breaking
(4) adj. (of arrangements, time, etc.) able to be altered to suit different needs

posExamples.sentence: When the sudden downpour ruined our outdoor plans, our teacher stayed remarkably flexible, turning the crowded classroom into the liveliest storytelling session we had ever had. （读后续写·师生·应变）
I would suggest that the schedule be made more flexible, so that students with different talents can arrange their study time in a way that best suits them. （应用文·建议信）
In a world that changes faster than ever, those who remain flexible in thought and open to new ideas are far more likely to thrive than those who cling to old certainties. （议论文·适应变化）
The gymnast's body was astonishingly flexible, bending and folding with a grace that made the impossible look effortless. （读后续写·体育·惊叹）

collocations.example: The company's flexible working hours allowed young parents to balance their careers with the needs of their children. （应用文·报道 / 说明）
A flexible approach to problem-solving often achieves what stubborn persistence cannot. （议论文·方法论）
"I can be flexible about the date," she offered warmly, sensing how tightly packed her friend's week already was. （读后续写·体贴·对话）
The plan was flexible enough to absorb last-minute changes, which proved a blessing when the weather suddenly turned. （读后续写·活动·顺利）
A flexible timetable would give us the freedom to pursue our hobbies without falling behind in our studies. （应用文·建议）
Wise as she was, she kept her options flexible, refusing to burn any bridges before the final decision. （读后续写·人物·睿智）
Even under mounting pressure, the captain remained flexible, adjusting the team's strategy the moment the situation shifted. （读后续写·领导·冷静）
Engineers chose flexible materials for the bridge so that it could sway safely in strong winds instead of snapping. （议论文·科技 / 说明）

synonyms.example: Highly adaptable, the new student blended into the strange environment within days, making friends where others would have felt lost. （读后续写·转学·融入）
synonyms.usage: 侧重能主动适应新环境或变化,多形容人或生物的适应性;flexible 既可指人也可指安排、材料,含义更广

synonyms.example: A versatile actor, he could switch from comedy to tragedy in a single breath, leaving the audience spellbound. （读后续写·才华·惊艳）
synonyms.usage: 强调多方面的能力或多种用途;flexible 强调可弯曲、可变通,不必然指"多才"

synonyms.example: The rules proved surprisingly elastic, stretching to accommodate every unexpected circumstance. （议论文·制度·弹性）
synonyms.usage: 本义指物理弹性,引申指规则、计划可伸缩调整;flexible 更常用于日常"灵活变通"之意

advancedExpressions.expression: flexible yet firm, sb. ...
advancedExpressions.example: Flexible yet firm, she adapted her methods to every child while never once bending on her core principle: no one would be left behind. （形容词短语前置 + yet 对比,续写塑造立体人物）

advancedExpressions.expression: it would be advisable to make ... more flexible so that ...
advancedExpressions.example: It would be advisable to make the club's rules more flexible so that members with heavy academic loads can still take part. （it would be advisable to 委婉建议 + so that 目的状语,应用文标准句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: those who stay flexible ..., whereas those who ...
advancedExpressions.example: Those who stay flexible in the face of change often turn crises into opportunities, whereas those who rigidly resist are swept aside by the tide of the times. （whereas 对比句 + 隐喻 tide of the times,议论文两面论证）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She was flexible and changed her plan.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Rather than clinging stubbornly to her original plan, she chose to stay flexible, reshaping her approach the instant she saw that the old one no longer served. （读后续写·抉择·成熟）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Rather than 让步开篇对比僵化 + cling stubbornly 反衬灵活 + reshape 动词升级 + the instant 引导时间从句强化应变的敏捷

sentenceUpgrade.original: Being flexible is important in modern life.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: In an age of relentless change, the capacity to remain flexible — to bend without breaking, to adapt without losing one's core — has become not merely an asset but a necessity for survival. （议论文·抽象升华）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: In an age of 时代背景开篇 + capacity to remain flexible 名词化主语 + 破折号排比(bend without breaking, adapt without losing) + not merely...but 递进拔高结论

translation: 账户；描述；解释；认为是，视为
sub_section: Extended reading
original_sentence: Mama and Her Bank Account Every Saturday night Mama would sit down by the kitchen table and count out the money Papa had brought home.
readingExamples: Mama and Her Bank Account Every Saturday night Mama would sit down by the kitchen table and count out the money Papa had brought home.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a written or spoken description of an event, giving details of what happened
(2) n. an arrangement with a bank to keep your money there and take it out when you need it
(3) n. a record of the money a person or business has received and spent
(4) vt. to consider or regard someone or something in a particular way

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 认为，视为（较正式，常用被动 be accounted）
uncommonMeanings.example: In that remote village, a man who could read and write was accounted a scholar, and the old teacher was treated with a reverence bordering on worship. （读后续写·乡村敬学）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 缘故，理由（用于 on account of / on this account 等）
uncommonMeanings.example: On account of the sudden storm, the mountain rescue team was forced to abandon the search until dawn, though not a single member had wanted to turn back. （读后续写·山地救援）

posExamples.sentence: Trembling, the boy gave a breathless account of how he had dragged his little sister from the icy river, his voice cracking as the frozen memory came rushing back. （读后续写·英雄叙事）
Enclosed is a detailed account of the charity fund, listing every donation received and every yuan spent, so that all members may see exactly where their generosity has gone. （应用文·公开信）
History accounts him one of the greatest reformers of his age, yet in his own lifetime he was mocked, misunderstood and driven into exile. （议论文·历史人物评价）
Every Saturday my grandmother would open a battered notebook and count out the coins, keeping a faithful account of the family's meagre earnings. （读后续写·家庭记忆）

idioms.example: A wise leader must take into account not only the profit of the moment but the well-being of generations yet unborn. （议论文·领导力）

idioms.translation: 决不，绝对不（否定副词置句首常倒装）
idioms.example: On no account should you reveal the surprise to Grandma before her birthday, whispered Mum, pressing a finger to her lips. （读后续写·对话/悬念）

idioms.idiom: give a good account of oneself
idioms.example: Though the youngest player on the pitch, Tom gave a good account of himself, chasing every ball as if the whole match rested on his shoulders. （读后续写·赛场拼搏）

collocations.translation: 解释；（比例）占；说明……的原因
collocations.example: How do you account for the fact that so many students, despite endless revision, still freeze the moment the exam begins? （议论文·教育反思）
The day I opened my first bank account, my father handed me a single coin and said the rest was up to me. （读后续写·成长节点）
Her diary offered a vivid account of the flood, so lifelike that readers could almost hear the water clawing at the doors. （读后续写·灾难叙事）
By all accounts, the old lighthouse keeper had never once abandoned his post, not even on the wildest of nights. （读后续写·人物传说）
At the end of each month Mama would settle the accounts at the kitchen table, her brow furrowed over every last cent. （读后续写·家庭生计）

collocations.translation: 追究某人责任，要某人担责
collocations.example: A truly just society holds its powerful to account, refusing to let wealth or status place anyone above the law. （议论文·公平正义）
The picnic was called off on account of the relentless rain that had soaked the field overnight. （应用文·通知）
To the proud minister the beggar's plea seemed of no account, yet that single dismissal would one day cost him everything. （读后续写·因果转折）

synonyms.example: The witness's calm description of the accident helped the police piece together exactly what had happened. （应用文·报告）
